messages:
maya: Hey team — customer (AcmeCorp) reporting sudden spike of 429s starting ~2026-01-10 for EU region. They say requests briefly succeed then we see a failover to US which increases latency and their bill. Can we triage?

jared: Thanks Maya. Do we have a sample request_id or trace id from their side? Also want to confirm: are they on Dedicated or Hosted?

maya: Hosted (standard plan). Customer pasted this header from one failed response: `x-request-id: req_0f9a3b2e`, timestamped ~1765509000. They included response headers: `x-region: eu-west-1`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-fallback-region: us-east-1`.

rachna: /cc @jared @cory I can pull routing logs for that timeframe. Quick Q: are they using multi-region routing or pinned to eu? They say default routing but prefer eu.

maya: They said they didn't pin. Just calling the host endpoint with region header unset.

jared: Ok. Two likely causes: (1) regional capacity hit (quota exhausted for eu pool) causing automated cross-region fallback, (2) an account-level burst limit applied. Need to check per-customer quota usage and per-region tokens/sec.

ops-bot: Incident alert: auto-throttle triggered in eu-west-1 2026-01-10T14:15:23Z — 429 spike > threshold (5m moving average). Fallback routing to us-east-1 enabled.

cory: Do we show any backend overload or pod OOMs in eu at that time? If runtime evicted KV caches it would increase token compute and could push past reserved capacity.

rachna: I checked node metrics: no OOMs, but GPU utilization hit 95% for 3 mins on the dedicated-shared eu pool. We had a bursty customer (internal test) around the same time. That could explain the temporary quota exhaustion.

jared: Can we repro locally with a synthetic burst to confirm fallback behavior? Steps to repro for support: 1) send 10x normal QPS from eu IP, 2) watch response headers for `x-rate-limit-reason` or `x-fallback-region`, 3) collect first request id that gets 429. Example curl:```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete -d '{"prompt":"test","max_tokens":10}'; done
```

maya: I'll try that with their key in a shadow environment and paste the logs here. Also they asked why billing jumped — if requests route to us-east it's charged at their plan's regional price?

cory: Billing note: cross-region fallbacks are billed at the region that served the request. If the account doesn't have reserved eu capacity, fallback to US uses hosted pool pricing which can vary. That explains their cost bump.

rachna: Quick fix options: (A) set `region: eu-west-1` pin in customer's config to avoid fallback (but if eu capacity is saturated they'd get 429s instead of higher-latency success), (B) offer short-term Dedicated burst capacity in eu, (C) increase per-minute quota for this customer if safe. Which do we want to recommend?

maya: Customer prefers lower latency > occasional 429s. They asked for canary-like behavior: prefer 429 over cross-region fallback. Can we flip policy?

jared: There is a routing policy flag `allow_cross_region_fallback` (default true). Ops can flip it per-customer via the Routing UI or API. If they prefer strict regional adherence, set it to false. Note: that may increase 429 surface area during eu saturation.

maya: Cool. I will propose: set `allow_cross_region_fallback=false` + short term quota bump for the next 24h while they complete load smoothing. Also ask billing to waive spike if it's from our routing default?

cory: I'll open a billing ticket and flag for review. Also will create a short-lived Dedicated reservation offer for eu to propose.

rachna: Action items: (1) Maya — repro in shadow env and paste `req_*` ids (due in 2h), (2) Jared — pull routing logs and confirm whether fallback was triggered by our auto-policy or user config (done), (3) Cory — billing ticket and new offer.

deploy-bot: Deploy notice: routing-policy service v2.18 rolled 2026-01-09 03:22 UTC — no config changes expected.

maya: Repro attempt: ran burst from our shadow key, got initial 429s with headers: `x-rate-limit-reason: region_quota_exhausted`, `x-fallback-region: us-east-1` for ~18s then resumed. Pasted one sample failed response:```json
{"error":"rate_limit","message":"region_quota_exhausted","request_id":"req_0f9a3b2e"}
```

jared: Verified — fallback is automatic when `region_quota_exhausted`. I'll add an internal note to surface `x-rate-limit-scope` more prominently in docs.

maya: Customer accepted the plan: flip fallback off and grant 2x quota for 12h. I'll make the config change and confirm. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

cory: Billing ticket created #BILL-1984, asked for spike review and potential partial credit.

rachna: Marking thread resolved once Maya confirms change and customer sees lower p95 for eu.

maya: Update — changed `allow_cross_region_fallback=false` at 1765510205, tested, they now get 429s instead of failover, latency fixed. Customer will smooth traffic. Closing in 24h if stable.
